- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. The premise of the question is incorrect. There is no "nightly database-cleanup job" configured in this repository's cron scheduler. The `internal/scheduler/` package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`) is a general-purpose cron job scheduling library — it does not define any application-specific jobs itself. The only "cleanup" reference is in an illustrative **example test** (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:97-106`), which shows a hypothetical `"cleanup"` job scheduled at `"0 2 * * *"` (2:00 AM) with the comment "Cleanup old data every night at 2 AM." This is sample/documentation code demonstrating how to use the scheduler API, not an actual scheduled database-cleanup job in the application.
